title: A finite local fibre dimension bounds a neighbourhood
statement: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let x ∈ X and d ∈ ℕ. Assume that the local topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] at the point of the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] over f(x) corresponding to x equals d. Then there exists an open neighbourhood W of x in X such that the local dimension of the fibre of f at every z ∈ W is at most d. No quasi-compactness, properness, Noetherian, flatness or finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 02FZ, affine reduction to Algebra Tag 00QH

proof.text: Choose an affine open T = Spec R of Y containing f(x) and an affine open W = Spec B of its inverse image containing x. The restriction h : W → T is locally of finite type, so its coordinate map R → B is finite type, by the affine characterization of def-weil-finite-type-morphism and def-weil-affine-spectrum.

source.place: Tag 02FZ, affine reduction; Tag 01T2, label lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize, affine-cover condition (4)

proof.text: For every $y\in W$, put $s=f(y)$. The fibre homeomorphisms in [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identify the fibre of $h$ over $s$ with the open subspace $W\cap f^{-1}(s)$ of $f^{-1}(s)$, the underlying space of $X_s$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] identifies its local dimension at the point over $y$ with $\dim_{\widetilde y}X_s$. Apply [lem-sbc-affine-coordinate-fibre-dimension] to $h$: if $\mathfrak q_y\subset B$ corresponds to $y$ and $\mathfrak p_y$ is its contraction to $R$, this common dimension is $\dim_{\mathfrak q_y}(B/R)$, measured on $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p_y))$. The affine comparison writes the tensor factors in the opposite order; the swap $b\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes b$ has its own inverse and carries the kernel of $b\otimes a\mapsto\bar b\bar a$ to the same distinguished prime. Its spectrum homeomorphism carries open neighbourhoods and chains of irreducible closed subsets bijectively, so preserves the defining minimum of dimensions.

source.place: Tag 02FZ, affine reduction; Schemes Tag 01K1, label lemma-fibre-topological; Algebra Tag 00E6, label remark-fundamental-diagram; Topology Tag 0055, label definition-Krull, item (4)

proof.text: The assumed equality says that the local fibre dimension at x is d. By the affine comparison of step 2, apply lem-weil-pbc-fibre-dimension-bounded-open-upstairs to the coordinate prime of x and d. Obtain an open neighbourhood V in the coordinate spectrum on which all local fibre dimensions are at most d.

source.place: Tag 00QH, label lemma-dimension-fibres-bounded-open-upstairs; relative dimension defined in Tag 00QD, label definition-relative-dimension

proof.text: Pull V back along the affine isomorphism of W with its coordinate spectrum and include the resulting open into X. This gives an open neighbourhood N of x. For each y in N, the open-subspace and coordinate comparisons of step 2 identify its local fibre dimension with a coordinate local fibre dimension bounded by d, proving the required bound.

theorem exists_bounded_fibre_dimension_neighbourhood
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (x : X) (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDimAt (f.asFiber x) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ∃ W : X.Opens, x ∈ W ∧
      ∀ z ∈ W, topologicalKrullDimAt (f.asFiber z) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)
